purpose: Define one recoverable, provider-observed release lifecycle for Callisto so that a reviewed managed release merge automatically releases exactly its committed version, can be resumed safely after interruption, and never treats workflow structure or local state as proof of publication.
scope: The Callisto release domain model, graph coordinator, CLI, GitHub Actions adapter, binary assets, behavioral test harness, rehearsal profile, release documentation, and merge governance required before the next self-release.
non_goals: A second manual approval or a GitHub Environment reviewer gate.
Publishing a new version merely to recover an unpublished merged version.
Treating a local execution-state file as the authority for remote publication.
Apple Developer signing, notarization, or an owner-specific certificate before a project policy and safe credential model exist.
Inventing a staging registry endpoint, credentials, or external service that the owner has not provisioned.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A verified merge of a managed release PR is the only publication authorization; the release workflow contains no GitHub Environment assignment, required-reviewer gate, or equivalent second approval.

Release orchestration is modeled by a serializable run envelope that records the exact orchestration revision, release-source revision, immutable intent digest, selected profile, and artifact-manifest digest.

A recovery invocation accepts an explicit full release-source SHA, verifies it is an allowed merged managed-release commit, creates fresh intent and artifacts from that source, and does not invoke versioning or create a version PR.

The current Callisto CLI and workflow revision remain distinct from the checked-out release source during recovery; tests prove that a post-failure orchestration fix can recover an older unpublished release source.

All release lifecycle semantics--source validation, provenance, planning, observation, transition selection, resume, terminality, receipt construction, and artifact-slot validation--have one CLI/graph owner; Actions only supplies scheduling, isolated checkouts, artifact transport, credentials to execute, and command invocation.

Before every effect and on every resume, each registry publication, Git tag, forge release, and artifact upload is provider-observed as absent, exact success, conflict, or indeterminate; indeterminate and conflict states fail closed with typed diagnostics.

An exact pre-existing remote effect is recorded as already satisfied without attempting a duplicate publication; a same-identity version whose remote contents do not match the immutable intent is reported as a conflict.

A process interruption after persisting Attempting can be resumed on a fresh runner with no prior local state by reconstructing progress from the immutable run envelope and provider observations; it cannot return success while any operation is incomplete.

A release receipt is emitted only after every required operation is provider-observed as terminal success or already satisfied, and the receipt includes provenance and per-operation observation evidence.

The production release plan includes attested binary asset slots for aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and wasm32-wasip1; each validated asset is attached to the product-level GitHub Release.

A release profile is consumed by the release lifecycle, has one production destination and isolated rehearsal destinations, and rejects shared forge destinations or registry endpoints before any effect.

Executable behavioral tests cover fresh release, recovery, hidden and nested artifact transport, clean source worktrees, source/orchestration identity separation, job-local Git credentials, no-secret plan/build jobs, partial provider success, provider conflict, and receipt emission; line-oriented YAML checks remain only as narrow policy guards.
The repository requires the concrete verification checks used as release evidence before merge, while merge remains the sole release authorization boundary.

Documentation, CLI help, configuration examples, tests, and workflow behavior describe the same release lifecycle; obsolete preview-only release paths are removed rather than retained as a second implementation.

revision_note: This structural specification supersedes piecemeal recovery workflow patches. It preserves already-correct no-approval and terminality fixes but requires the unconsumed profile model and workflow-only provenance handoff to be either integrated into the canonical lifecycle or removed.
reasoning: Grounded in the owner-authoritative incident report and live source inspection on 2026-09-17. External staging registry selection remains intentionally unresolved rather than fabricated.
